report.tagline: A dating app 'designed to be deleted', where you like a specific photo or answer on someone's profile instead of swiping.
report.simpleSummary: Hinge is a dating app for people who want a relationship, not just a match. Every profile has photos plus three short prompts, like 'My most irrational fear is...'. Instead of swiping, you like or comment on one specific thing, which makes starting a chat easy. It is owned by Match Group, the same company as Tinder, and it is the fastest-growing big dating app, making money from paid plans that show who likes you and give better placement.

keyNumbers.label: Annual revenue
keyNumbers.value: About $650 million in 2025; on track for $1 billion in 2027
keyNumbers.note: 2025 figure is our estimate from Match Group filings. The $1 billion 2027 target was repeated by management in November 2026.

keyNumbers.label: Monthly active users growth, Q3 2026
keyNumbers.note: Match Group Q3 2026 earnings call. Absolute users not disclosed.

keyNumbers.label: Payer penetration
keyNumbers.note: Match Group Q3 2026: a smaller share of Hinge users pay, leaving room to grow.

overview.whatItDoes: Hinge matches people looking for serious dating. Profiles combine six photos or videos with three written or voice prompts. Users send likes or comments on a specific part of a profile, which leads to better first messages and, Hinge says, more dates.
howItWorks: Sign up, add six photos or videos, three prompts and details like religion, height and dating intentions.
Browse the Discover feed, one profile at a time.
Like or comment on a specific photo or prompt; the other person sees what you liked.
If they like you back, you match and chat.
Paid tiers, Hinge+ and HingeX, show everyone who liked you, unlimited likes and priority placement.
Roses are special likes used for 'Standouts', which are highly compatible profiles.
overview.valueProposition: Fewer but better matches, with real conversations, for people who want a relationship.

painPoints.pain: Swiping apps feel shallow and lead to low-effort messages like 'hi'.
painPoints.howSolved: Liking a specific prompt or photo gives an easy, personal starting point.

painPoints.pain: Too many matches with no real conversation.
painPoints.howSolved: Daily like limits and 'Your Turn' reminders push people to reply instead of collecting matches.

painPoints.pain: Hard to know if someone wants the same thing.
painPoints.howSolved: Profiles show dating intentions, such as 'long-term relationship'.

painPoints.pain: People don't know how to write a good profile.
painPoints.howSolved: Prompt Feedback, an AI tool, suggests how to make answers more specific.

painPoints.pain: Searching for compatible people takes time.
painPoints.howSolved: Most Compatible and Standouts suggest people based on past likes.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Three short questions answered in text or voice on every profile.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Shows personality and gives an easy way to start talking. It is Hinge's signature design.

coreFeatures.feature: Likes and comments on specific content
coreFeatures.whatItDoes: You like one photo or prompt and can add a comment.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Leads to more replies than a blind swipe.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Daily suggestions of highly compatible people; Standouts need a Rose to like.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Improves match quality and sells Roses.

coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Paid plans: see all likes, unlimited likes, advanced filters; HingeX adds priority and skip-the-line.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Main source of revenue at about $30 per payer a month.

coreFeatures.feature: Your Turn Limits and Match Note
coreFeatures.whatItDoes: Limits how many chats wait on you, and lets you leave a note when unmatching.
coreFeatures.whyItMatters: Reduces ghosting, where someone stops replying without warning.

steps.detail: Hears from friends that Hinge is for 'serious' dating.
Adds photos and picks prompts; uses AI feedback to improve one answer.
Comments on a man's answer about his favourite street food.
He likes her back and replies to the comment.
They meet after a few days of chatting.
Runs out of free daily likes.
Sees he has likes but cannot see them all.
Sees Hinge+ and HingeX with weekly, monthly and 3-month prices.
If he meets someone, he deletes the app, which is the goal.

userJourneys.name: Deleting the app after meeting someone

steps.detail: Sees the same person over weeks.
Hides her profile while exploring the relationship.
Hinge asks 'We met?' to learn which matches turned into dates.
Deletes the app, true to its 'designed to be deleted' line.
Tells single friends, which brings new users.

businessModel.summary: Hinge makes money from paid plans, Hinge+ and HingeX, plus one-off purchases like Roses and Boosts. About $30 a month per payer. The goal of helping users leave sounds strange, but happy couples bring friends, and singles keep joining.

revenueStreams.detail: Hinge+ and HingeX, bought weekly, monthly or for several months. Most of revenue.

businessModel.pricing: Free to start. In the US, Hinge+ is often around $30 to $35 a month and HingeX around $50, with discounts for longer plans. Prices vary by market and are shown in-app.
costDrivers: App store fees of up to 30%
businessModel.unitEconomics: One payer brings about $30 a month. Up to $9 can go to app stores. Running the app costs a little per user. A payer who stays 3 months brings about $60 to $65 after fees. Because users leave when they find someone, Hinge depends on steady new sign-ups and referrals, not long subscriptions.

howTheyGetUsers: Word of mouth from couples who met on Hinge
Brand campaigns about being 'designed to be deleted'
Expansion into new countries in Europe and Latin America
Users switching from Tinder and Bumble
growth.moat: Hinge owns the 'serious dating' brand among young professionals. Its data on which matches lead to dates improves its suggestions. Being part of Match Group gives it money and know-how.

competitors.name: Tinder
competitors.positioning: Swipe app, casual image, largest pool.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Hinge is slower, more personal and focused on relationships.

competitors.name: Bumble
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Hinge lets anyone start, with prompts; Bumble is shrinking.

competitors.name: Aisle and matrimony sites
competitors.positioning: Indian apps for serious relationships and marriage.
competitors.howThisProductDiffers: Hinge is casual-serious and global; Aisle and Shaadi are more family and marriage focused.

northStar.metric: Weekly number of matches that lead to a date (users confirming 'We met')
northStar.why: Hinge promises to get you off the app. Dates are the clearest proof it is working.

improvementIdeas.idea: After a chat passes 20 messages, suggest a date with two nearby venues and a one-tap 'Want to meet?' card
improvementIdeas.problem: Many good chats stall before anyone suggests meeting, which breaks Hinge's 'designed to be deleted' promise.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More chats turn into dates, and happy users bring friends.

improvementIdeas.idea: Give every free user one Rose a week to send to a Standout
improvementIdeas.problem: Free users complain they feel invisible unless they pay for HingeX.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More matches for free users, better retention, and a taste of paid features that can lift upgrades.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Day-30 retention of free users and Hinge+ conversion

improvementIdeas.idea: Launch in Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru with college and workplace campaigns and filters for religion, language and family plans
improvementIdeas.problem: Indian users report a small pool outside a few metros, so matches dry up.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: A bigger local pool and more matches per user in India.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Monthly active users and matches per user in Indian metros

improvementIdeas.idea: Nudge users to close or reply to chats older than 3 days, with a ready-made Match Note
improvementIdeas.problem: Ghosting is a top complaint and makes people leave dating apps.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer dead chats and more replies.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Ghosting rate (chats with no reply after 72 hours)

improvementIdeas.idea: Free safety check: require a video selfie before sending a comment
improvementIdeas.problem: Fake profiles and scams reduce trust, especially for women.
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: Fewer scam reports and more women staying active.
improvementIdeas.metricToTrack: Scam reports per 1,000 users and women's retention

pmLessons: A strong promise, 'designed to be deleted', can build trust and growth.
Small design choices, like liking a specific prompt, change user behaviour.
Measuring real-world outcomes like dates keeps the team focused on value.

interviewQuestions.question: Hinge wants users to delete it. How can it still grow revenue to $1 billion?
interviewQuestions.hint: Break revenue into new users x payer share x revenue per payer x months paid. Show how referrals from couples, new countries and short weekly plans fill the funnel even when users leave.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Hinge's north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Pick dates (confirmed through 'We met'), not matches or likes. Explain why, then break it into profile quality, match rate, conversations and dates, with a guardrail on safety.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce ghosting on Hinge?
interviewQuestions.hint: Define ghosting with a number, find causes (too many chats, low interest), test changes to Your Turn Limits or nudges, and track reply rates plus a guardrail on time spent.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Hinge launch a big push in India?
interviewQuestions.hint: Size the market of urban singles, look at culture and competitors like Aisle and matrimony sites, decide pricing in rupees, and pick a launch metric such as matches per user in the first city.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you test whether prompts beat photos for starting conversations?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare reply rate and date rate for likes on prompts vs likes on photos, control for profile quality, and run an A/B test on prompt placement.
